title: After 20 years of coding, I made my first video game !
author: jyuukie
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been a developer for over **20 years**, but until recently, I'd never made my own video game.

So I decided to try. :)

The project started as a small experiment with a lone Wanderer facing a huge creature. Now it's **Endless Duel, a free browser roguelite with 10 chapters!**

You fight colossal bosses in turn-based combat with active parries, strikes, and special techniques. **If you die, you return to Chapter I, but you keep what you've earned.** You can also collect cards and care for pets!

I built the game with the help of several AI tools:

* **Claude Code & Codex** for development
* **ChatGPT Images** for illustrations
* **Strudel** for music
* **ElevenLabs** for some sounds and voices

The game itself runs on **TypeScript and PixiJS**.

But what I enjoyed most was exploring everything beyond programming: game design, art direction, animations, music, sound design... Things I'd always wanted to try!

And yes, I spent far too much time trying to get a katana sound just right. :)

Of course, I didn't just ask AI to "make me a game". There was plenty of planning, reviewing, experimenting, and starting over.

One thing I've learned: **good structure makes ambitious projects much easier to manage when working with AI agents.**

Anyway, you can play Endless Duel for free on desktop and mobile:

⚔️ [**https://endlessduel.com/**](https://endlessduel.com/?ref=reddit)

I'd love to hear from other AI game developers. **How do you keep code, visuals, and gameplay consistent when using different tools?**

And of course, any feedback on the game is welcome!

comments.author: djmisterjon
comments.body:
Sorry, but the page froze for over 6 seconds. I had to leave and close it.

People have become impatient, and UX needs to adapt. Every second of friction can cost you a user.

replies.author: jyuukie
replies.body: Oh really ? I will check this, it should not happens. Maybe the first loading is too long...

replies.author: djmisterjon
replies.body:
You could try loading a UI or some async content around the loading process. That's what I do for my Unity demos.  
[https://jonlepage.github.io/LSDEDE-runtime/](https://jonlepage.github.io/LSDEDE-runtime/)

On my end, everything was frozen and nothing was progressing (i use Vivaldi browser chromium based).  
My first reaction was that it was a bug, so I closed it without even waiting.  
Many people are impatient, like me, when staring at a static image with nothing happening.🙄

replies.author: jyuukie
replies.body: Thanks for that feedback ! I will check.

comments.author: throwaway09234023322
comments.body: Very cool visuals and design. No feedback really because I mostly only enjoy strategy type games

comments.author: Traditional_End_743
comments.body:
The visuals look amazing and really consistent. Kudos for that!

Did you generate your spritesheets from ChatGPT images? I'm curious about your process/pipeline!

replies.author: jyuukie
replies.body:
Thank you ! Yes exactly. I use codex with ChatGPT images to generate the artworks and I've created quite a few custom skills to build a proper production harness around the whole process.

The idea is to keep everything consistent, from art direction and character proportions to animations and asset integration.

comments.body: Yo this is really fkn cool!! I only played the first battle (too busy rn) but the concept seems really satisfying so far.  Is it alright if I DM you so we can talk dev strategies and workflows? I’m working on a tactical strategy rpg right now

comments.author: Adro_95
comments.body:
Feedback from a gamer, not a developer. 
The idea is good, a type of gameplay i've never tried yet.
The artworks and the musics are super cool.
The only thing i would point out (which probably is exactly how you wanted to design the game) is that it's an actual endless fight without meta-progression. Usually in this type of games you get some kind of reward for doing a good run, something you carry over your career
